newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians would accept divided Jerusalem -poll.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians would accept divided Jerusalem -poll.

text.p: A majority of Palestinians would accept dividing Jerusalem into two separate cities, one Arab and the other Israeli, a poll conducted by a U.S. university showed on Thursday.

Almost 70 percent of the 807 Palestinians polled in the University of Maryland survey said they would consider dividing the city, while a little more than half said they could share Jerusalem with Israel.
Israel captured Arab East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war and declared all of the holy city its "eternal and indivisible" capital.
The PLO wants East Jerusalem as the capital of a Palestinian state and the issue of Jewish settlement-building in the city has plunged Israeli-Palestinian peacemaking into crisis.
Almost all of the Palestinians questioned said they could never accept sole Israeli sovereignty over Jerusalem even if Israel agreed to a Palestinian state in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
"That's a total non-starter. Ninety-four percent of Palestinians said no," study author Jerome Segal told reporters.
Control of holy sites brought some of the most vehement reactions.

The survey showed that 70 percent of Palestinians want Moslem religious authorities to control Jerusalem's Haram al-Sharif, known to Jews as the Temple Mount, which includes the Dome of the Rock and al-Aqsa mosques.
Nearly 80 percent said Jews should not be allowed to pray on the mount, the site of the biblical Jewish temples.
"Very few Palestinians believe that Jews have any legitimate rights to Jerusalem," said Nader Sa'id, who co-authored the study with Segal.
Palestinians said they would recognise Israeli sovereignty over the Western Wall, Judaism's holiest site, if Israel recognised Palestinian control of Haram al-Sharif.
But Segal said Israelis, whom he polled last year, rejected this.
Both sides did agree that they should stop arguing over sovereignty and agree in principle that ultimate authority over holy sites belongs to God.

About 64 percent of Palestinians and 35 percent of Israelis supported the idea, with the most religious giving it the most vehement backing. Secular Jews and Palestinians opposed the move, the survey showed.
